mechanism_narrative: A low level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% signals economic weakness and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above their 3-month moving averages indicates robust economic momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and PAYEMS above 3-month moving average
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and PAYEMS are above their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening economic momentum, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC for INDPRO change in late-cycle is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High annualized inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals monetary policy tightening and reduced real returns, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and monthly retail sales (RSAFS) above their respective growth thresholds indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 0.5% and RSAFS monthly growth > 0.3%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when both GDPC1 and RSAFS growth thresholds are met, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS is above its 12-month average, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.0% for three consecutive months signals monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.0% for three consecutive months, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
